text:
maria: I uploaded a perfetto trace for a 50-concurrent reqs run — seeing a weird 300-450ms tail on end-to-end latency. can someone take a quick look? https://perfetto.app/trace/?url=redwood/trace/1786594321

kai: looking now. tl;dr: gateway->runtime span looks fine until runtime scheduling, then long gap before kernels start.

devon: I grabbed a couple screenshots. runtime main thread shows 'kernel_selection' NVTX bracket that ends ~120ms before first cudaLaunch. then a big memcpy and a bunch of small kernels.

anya: that kernel_selection gap smells like batched request combinatorics — maybe heuristic picked a suboptimal kernel and then fell back? also KV cache miss storm could cause extra CPU work.

maria: annotated the trace with CPU stacks for the gap. see: UI -> CPU slices -> select_kernels -> compute_quantized_layout.

devon: fwiw I also see L2 cache thrash markers on the GPU timeline right after the first kernels land. could be memory layout mismatch from quantized kernel selection.

trace-bot: perfetto parsed: summary: 50 reqs, p50 62ms, p95 212ms, p99 378ms, max 468ms. Top CPU hotspots: select_kernels, kv_lookup_miss_handler, memcpy_async_enqueue.

kai: can you paste the perfetto flame view URL for the CPU slice?

maria: https://perfetto.app/trace/?q=1786594321#flame_view=cpu:slices:select_kernels

anya: quick hypothesis: new batching heuristic (commit 5b8c2f) tries to merge by prompt length and ends up computing layout for a large merged batch, then throws it away and reruns kernel selection for smaller shards. that extra compute is the gap.

devon: how to validate: repro with env var RW_RUNTIME_BATCH_DEBUG=1 to log batch plans and timings. also collect nsys with NVTX to correlate CPU/NV kernel launches.

maria: I've attached the short log excerpt from RW_RUNTIME_BATCH_DEBUG:

```
[2026-03-10 15:12:21.112] plan attempt=0 batch_size=48 expected_tokens=1024 compute_layout_time_ms=132
[2026-03-10 15:12:21.248] plan attempt=1 batch_size=12 expected_tokens=256 compute_layout_time_ms=14
[2026-03-10 15:12:21.267] kernel_selection_ms=10 selected_variant=quant4x4
[2026-03-10 15:12:21.280] kv_cache_miss_count=9 memcopy_enqueue_ms=18
```

kai: that lines up — first expensive plan then quick fallback. 132ms compute_layout is the big chunk we see. we need to know why first plan is attempted. maybe ordering by arrival timestamp causes the 48-batch path.

anya: action: (1) add a cheap precheck to reject overly-large layout attempts if expected_tokens > 768 and batch_size > 32, (2) instrument kernel selector to emit NVTX start/end around layout compute, (3) repro with nsys.

devon: nsys command I recommend:

```
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace_nsight -t nvtx,cuda,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --force-overwrite --trace-fork-before-exec true -- python -m server.bench --concurrency 50 --duration 30
```

kai: and for a CPU-side perf capture for the select_kernels path:

```
sudo perf record -F 200 -g -o /tmp/perf.data -- sleep 30
sudo perf script | flamegraph.pl > select_kernels.svg
```

maria: good. once we have nsys we can open in Nsight and jump from NVTX bracket 'layout_compute' to the CPU thread region in perfetto.

anya: also please dump KV cache metrics (hit/miss per-request). if there's a miss storm it inflates memcpy and kernel invocations. simple curl to /metrics shows aggregator totals but we want per-request histograms.

devon: quick workaround we can try in prod: reduce max_batch_window_ms from 30 -> 10 so fewer large speculative plans. that should drop compute_layout attempts under load while we fix logic.

maria: I'll run the nsys + RW_RUNTIME_BATCH_DEBUG repro on a reproducible nightly job and share traces. plan to add the layout-size precheck in a follow-up PR.

kai: assign follow-ups: maria -> collect traces and attach to issue; anya -> prototype precheck + NVTX markers; devon -> perf scripts and dashboard for KV miss per-request.

maria: thanks all, will post results. :rocket:
